title: Phase 1 NULL → third boundary condition: knowledge must be PROJECT-LOCAL (absent from pretraining)
summary: Phase 1 proxy-validation A/B (34 runs, complete): 4 reconstructed "transfer-robust winnable" tasks (native-store, claim-task, wt-gc, tls-local) + 3 controls — COLD PASSED EVERY HELD-OUT EDGE CASE on every task, zero variance. Proxy precision 0/4 (controls 3/3 correct). MECHANISM: the transfer-robust facts (mkcert issuer-trust, don't-clobber-native-files, worktree GC retention, stale-claim hygiene) are general engineering knowledge in the model's PRETRAINING PRIOR — memory cannot add value for facts the model already knows; tls-local's spec even names mkcert-install-ca in its step vocabulary and cold still needed no note. The n=1/n=2 WINS used PROJECT-LOCAL facts (this registry's ~40% missing-session rate; this feed's de-DE locale mix) that pretraining cannot cover. BOUNDARY now 3 conditions: empirical ∧ external-to-artifact ∧ PROJECT-LOCAL. This INVERTS Phase 0a's transfer reading: the 12/18 benchmark-meta winnable tasks (project-local measured verdicts) are exactly where memory wins, while the 6 general-infra ones are pretrained away. What transfers to a customer project is the CATEGORY — every project accumulates its own local empirical facts (their flaky test, their API quirk, their data feed) — at ~23% (12/52) of note-dependent tasks on this corpus (self-similarity caveat stands). Product implication: agent memory's value proposition is PROJECT-LOCAL scar tissue, not general knowledge curation; the gate should weight project-specificity signals (measured numbers, error strings, local paths/names) over topical relevance. bench/report-phase1.{md}; data bench/heldout/p1/results.jsonl. n=2 existence proof unchanged.
